mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE rising above 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and accelerating inflation, increasing real interest rates and compressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly increase in both personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 6-month averages signals strengthening household demand, which boosts consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST exceed their 6-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decrease in the unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE remains below 4% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS) above its 12-month average, combined with a simultaneous decline in personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1), signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS exceeds its 12-month moving average while GDPC1 is below its 12-month moving average.
